title: quant-tradeoff-playbook-int8-fp8-q4-draft
content:
Purpose:
A working draft for an internal quantization tradeoff calculator and recommendation playbook. Goal is to capture practical heuristics (INT8, FP8, 4-bit/Q4) that the Optimize team can use to estimate cost/latency/quality tradeoffs quickly and produce deterministic rollout recommendations for Dedicated and Private customers.

Status: draft, rough numbers, needs kernel-level profiling to validate. Use this as a planning artifact and not a final SLA.

Scope:
- Target models: 7B, 13B, 70B (common customer anchors) but formulas generalize.
- Quant modes covered: INT8 (symmetric/affine), FP8 (E4M3 or E5M2), and 4-bit (GPTQ-like Q4 variants).
- Metrics: memory footprint (weights), runtime latency per request, throughput (tokens/sec), and expected relative quality degradation (task-dependent).

Assumptions (baseline definitions):
- Baseline numeric format: FP16 weights and activation compute paths. Baseline memory reported = FP16 weight-only size (no KV cache).
- Typical baseline sizes used below: 7B FP16 = 14 GB, 13B FP16 = 26 GB, 70B FP16 = 140 GB (rounded, weight-only).
- Cloud/Dedicated GPU effective cost = variable (placeholder in examples).
- Latency/throughput multipliers are kernel-level estimates; actual depends on microkernels, cuBLAS/cutlass/fused ops and GPU generation.

Quick multiplier cheatsheet (conservative):
- INT8: size multiplier = 0.50x vs FP16; latency multiplier = 0.85x (i.e., faster); expected quality delta = -0.0% to -2.0% depending on task/prompt.
- FP8: size multiplier = 0.60x vs FP16; latency multiplier = 0.90x; expected quality delta = -0.0% to -1.0%.
- 4-bit (Q4/GPTQ): size multiplier = 0.25x vs FP16; latency multiplier = 0.75x (can be faster due to cache fit); expected quality delta = -2.0% to -8.0% (high variance).

Example model size table (rounded):
Model | FP16 | INT8 (~0.5x) | FP8 (~0.6x) | Q4 (~0.25x)
7B    | 14 GB | 7.0 GB       | 8.4 GB      | 3.5 GB
13B   | 26 GB | 13.0 GB      | 15.6 GB     | 6.5 GB
70B   | 140 GB| 70.0 GB      | 84.0 GB     | 35.0 GB

Latency & cost toy calculator (per-request):
Inputs required: baseline_latency_ms (FP16, median P50), tokens_per_request (avg tokens returned), GPU_hourly_cost_usd.
Formulas (single-request cost approximation):
- latency_quant_ms = baseline_latency_ms * latency_multiplier
- gpu_cost_per_ms = GPU_hourly_cost_usd / (3600 * 1000)
- cost_per_request_usd = latency_quant_ms * gpu_cost_per_ms
- cost_per_token_usd = cost_per_request_usd / tokens_per_request

Example numeric worked example (illustrative):
- Baseline: 13B FP16 median latency = 120 ms per request (single-stream), tokens_per_request = 64, GPU_hourly_cost_usd = $6.00 (example Dedicated rate).
Compute INT8:
- latency_int8_ms = 120 * 0.85 = 102 ms
- gpu_cost_per_ms = 6.00 / 3,600,000 = 0.0000016667 USD/ms
- cost_per_request_int8 = 102 * 0.0000016667 = $0.00017
- cost_per_token_int8 = 0.00017 / 64 = $2.7e-06 per token
Compare FP16 baseline cost per token:
- cost_per_request_fp16 = 120 * 0.0000016667 = $0.00020
- cost_per_token_fp16 = 0.00020 / 64 = $3.1e-06 per token
Relative unit cost reduction ~14% (driven by latency improvement + memory enabling higher concurrency).

Notes on memory vs concurrency: smaller weight footprint often improves achievable concurrency per-GPU (more model instances or larger batch sizes), so effective cost reduction can be multiplicative compared to per-request latency improvements. Example: INT8 halves memory so we can place 2x model instances in same GPU memory footprint, roughly doubling throughput if kernel/compute allow.

Quality guidance and evals:
- Always pair quant rollout with a targeted eval set that mirrors production prompts (prompt-mix + critical safety prompts).
- Alert triggers: task metric drop > 1% absolute for high-value classification/regression or > 2% relative BLEU/ROUGE/ExactMatch for NLU tasks. For open-ended generation, use a combination of embedding similarity thresholds and human reviews (tiered).
- Prefer FP8 for low-risk early rollback (smaller quality delta) where kernel support exists. Use INT8 when throughput/memory constraints force it and accuracy tolerances are lenient. Use Q4 for cost-first, accuracy-second workflows (embeddings, retrieval-augmented generation with strong re-rankers).

Calibration and engineering notes:
- Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) with per-channel scales and symmetric quantization typically gives best size/speed win with lowest quality loss.
- Some kernels require calibration datasets (representative tokens) to compute scales; always save calibration artifacts for reproducibility.
- Quantization-Aware Training (QAT) may be necessary for models where PTQ yields >3% quality loss on critical prompts. Plan the cost of QAT vs the cost savings in production.
- KV cache: quantization of KV cache (activation storage) has different implications; sometimes quantizing weights but keeping activations in FP16 reduces latency impact. Document per-kernel support.

Operational rollout checklist (recommendation):
1) Local kernel profiling: measure P50/P95 latency and memory for candidate quant modes on target GPU generation.
2) Run the production prompt set evaluation with automated metrics + 100 human spot checks.
3) Estimate per-token cost under conservative GPU pricing and concurrency assumptions.
4) Canary rollout to low-traffic route with circuit-breaker: automatic fallback to FP16 if error rate increases or quality thresholds trigger.
5) Monitor: latency, token cost, metric deltas, user complaints. Keep rollback window and runbook ready.

Edge cases and caveats:
- Some ops (LM head, softmax) may have numerics-sensitive paths; quantizing them can introduce instability. Test sequence lengths beyond expected to catch KV cache overflow-related artifacts.
- Mixed-precision strategies (e.g., FP16 weights + INT8 matmul kernels) can sometimes give best tradeoffs; document supported kernel combos per release.
- Model architecture matters: heavily-MLP models vs attention-heavy models may show different quantization sensitivity.

Open questions & experiments to run:
- Profile FP8 kernels across our fleet GPUs (A100, H100, top-of-rack equivalents) for microbenchmarks (matmul latency, memory bandwidth stalls).
- System-level throughput: measure how many concurrent streams per GPU for each quant mode under typical request patterns.
- Human evaluation matrix: define 200-500 critical prompts across product verticals for deterministic checks.
- Cost sensitivity analysis: run scenario analysis for GPU_price ∈ [$2, $12] and avg_tokens ∈ [16, 256].

Next steps (owners):
- Miguel: schedule kernel-level benchmarks for INT8/FP8 on H100 (due 2026-03-25).
- Sophie: assemble prompt-mix eval set and automation harness (due 2026-03-18).
- Ben: implement quick Google Sheets prototype of the calculator and integrate with per-region GPU price table (due 2026-03-22).

Appendix: quick reference formulas for spreadsheet users:
- size_quant = size_fp16 * size_multiplier
- latency_quant = latency_fp16 * latency_multiplier
- cost_per_request = (GPU_hourly_cost / 3600) * (latency_quant / 1000)  // convert ms to seconds in some sheets; double-check units
- tokens_per_second = tokens_per_request / (latency_quant / 1000)

Commentary (notes to self):
- Keep this doc in Drive as working artifacts; final playbook should be moved to Confluence and included in Console recommendations.
- Flagged for product review before customer-facing one-pager.

Unresolved items (for team discussion):
- Standardize multipliers per GPU gen and keep a single source of truth (should live in infra pricing + kernel matrix).
- Decision tree for when to recommend FP8 vs INT8 in the Console Optimize suggestions.

End of draft.
